source.title: Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay

confidence_rationale: Normative theory giving the priority rule (utility = gain x need) for WHICH transitions a credit sweep should update first; reproduces reverse-replay-after-reward. Directly upgrades REE's existing backward_credit_sweep (prioritise by utility/TD-error) -- extend, not duplicate. Theoretical, not a benchmark.
failure_signatures: An undirected per-step novelty bonus spreads learning uniformly; a utility-prioritised backward sweep concentrates updates on exactly the reward-relevant transitions, which is what makes replay efficient.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Replay accesses memories in order of utility (gain x need): 'gain' propagates a newly-encountered outcome backward to preceding states (reverse replay), 'need' evaluates imminent choices forward; this single prioritised-access rule reproduces empirical replay phenomenology and unifies planning, learning and consolidation.
mapping.ree_translation: Gives REE's existing backward_credit_sweep a priority rule -- order updates by utility/TD-error rather than uniform or recency-only -- so credit concentrates on the forage-reward-relevant transitions; the ML analog is prioritised sweeping / prioritised experience replay.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Normative model, not a performance benchmark on a forage task; the efficiency claim is theoretical + fits neural data, so 'closes the gap faster' is a strong hypothesis, not a measured delta.
mapping.source_context: Normative modelling of rodent hippocampal replay + human planning.

confidence_components.notes: High-value low-cost upgrade to machinery REE already has; prioritised queue is tiny in a small gridworld.
